kyteler_host.text: Welcome to Kyteler's. Dame Alice Kyteler lived here in the 1300s, a rich lady with four husbands and a head for business.
In 1324 she was accused of witchcraft, in the first big witch case recorded in Ireland. She escaped to England and was never caught.
Locals say the charges were really about her money. Some swear her ghost tidies the cellar, which is more than I do.

then.text: The pot's back on its hook, smelling faintly of leek and potato. The tourists think it adds to the atmosphere. Thank you.
Dame Alice was accused in 1324, with her maid Petronilla de Meath, who was burnt that November. It was the first witchcraft burning in Ireland. The pot is a prop, mind. I checked.
Well? Have you seen everything? Right then. Who took Petronilla's Pot?

Nuala, landlady. Eighteen years behind this bar and I have never lost a thing bigger than a corkscrew.

Till Tuesday. Petronilla's Pot is gone from over the hearth. Black iron, sixty litres, hung there longer than I have. The tourists say it was Dame Alice's own cauldron. I say it was a very large stew pot with good PR.
Four people had reason to care about it: the steward at Rothe House, the verger at St Canice's, the clerk at the Tholsel, and a certain lady with a cafe in the Butter Slip. I'll not say who is who.
Look at things, ask about, and read your Fieldbook's Casebook tab (Run cycles the tabs). Come back when you're sure. A wrong name costs you standing, and I will be sorry, but not very.
